documents.unit: Rutgers Office of Information Technology (all campuses)
documents.title: Guidance on the use of AI at Rutgers
documents.summary: Universitywide IT guidance covering all Rutgers campuses. Says AI use in academic settings varies by discipline, course and instructor, but that AI should not be treated as permitted for coursework unless instructors say so, and tells users to use approved tools, protect confidential data, verify output and follow purchasing and existing university policies.
documents.stance_why: The page leaves guidance to 'discipline, course, and/or instructor', but sets its own default for coursework: AI 'should not be considered permissible for coursework unless clearly stated or communicated by instructors'. That is banned unless explicitly permitted, so restrict rather than delegates.

units.why: The page says OIT 'provides access to generative AI tools with protections', which is a statement that the university supplies licensed tools; this fits P17 (sanctioned tool) and informs rather than binds.
units.anchor: provides access to generative AI tools with protections for use in university work.
units.fit_note: University-wide OIT-provided tools, not a course-specific tool.
units.resolution_why: Found by coder B only (A folded this sentence into its 'no model training' unit). Source: 'The Office of Information Technology (OIT) provides access to generative AI tools with protections for use in university work.' It states what the university provides, so it is a real policy statement (P17, informs); kept, with a fit note because the tool is university-wide, not course-specific.

units.why: The sentence 'your data will not be used to train the models underlying the tools' states a data-protection property of the approved tools. It is a fact (informs) addressed to anyone using them, and it belongs with protecting data and preferring vetted tools (P50).
units.anchor: your data will not be used to train the models underlying the tools
units.fit_note: Also states a data-protection benefit (no model training on user data), which P17 does not capture.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: actor admin, P17 permit; coder B: actor all, P50 neutral. The source sentence begins 'By using the Rutgers-approved versions of these tools, your data will not...' so it addresses users, not administrators, and its content is data protection, not the provision of a tool (which the preceding sentence, now a separate unit, covers). Final: all, P50, neutral.

documents.summary: An archived OTEAR page of advice for Rutgers faculty on responding to generative AI: learn the tools, redesign assignments and rubrics, write a clear course policy, and choose among three sample syllabus statements. Most of the page is event listings, FAQs and reading lists, and it says it is no longer maintained.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no rule of its own; it says 'Develop clear policies for each course' and offers three sample statements ranging from 'not permitted' to 'fully permitted', so the choice is handed to instructors and the statements are listed as tiers.

notes: Reconciled from coders A and B. Both documents are universitywide Rutgers pages shared across campuses; no Newark-specific, school or computing-unit AI policy found; course layer deferred. The OTEAR page is archived and points to the OIT page. Not coded: navigation, event listings, reading and tool lists, third-party items; the sample syllabus statements that repeat in the FAQ were coded once. Sample statements are coded as options offered to instructors (document stance delegates, tiers listed), not as mandated rules. Coder notes: A: Both documents are universitywide Rutgers pages shared across campuses; no Newark-specific or computing-unit AI policy. The OTEAR page is marked archived/unmaintained and points to the OIT page. Many linked resources and reading lists on the OTEAR page were not coded as policy. B: Coder B. Only the two included universitywide documents were coded. Not coded: OTEAR navigation, event descriptions, reading and tool lists (links to third-party items, not Rutgers policy). The OTEAR page is marked archived and no longer maintained. The three sample syllabus statements appear twice on the page; the repeat in the FAQ was not coded again. Sample statements are coded as options offered to instructors, not as mandated rules.
